MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  JUNE 15, 2020

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates
  was called to order at 6:04 p.m. in George F Canyon Nature Center (Deck Area) 27305 Palos
  Verdes Drive East, Rolling Hills Estates, California by CHAIR PERSICHINA.

  2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR PERSICHINA led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Persichina, Pope, Bain, Romanelli, Ciarolla, Retz

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  McCormick

  STAFF PRESENT:  Alexa Davis, Assistant City Manager
  Michael Goldsmith, Maintenance Superintendent
  Cynthia Morquecho, Comm. Services Supervisor
  Daniel A-Haja, Community Services Coordinator

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF
  MAY 18, 2020

  COMMISSIONER BAIN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK
  to:

  APPROVE THE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF MAY 18,
  2020.

  There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  None

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  None

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  PVPLC ANNUAL REPORT (VERBAL REPORT)
  This item will be discussed following Item 8B.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
JUNE 15, 2020
   8.  ADJOURN TO THE PEPPERTREE FOUNDATION ADVISORY BOARD MEETING

  CHAIR PERSICHINA made a motion due to:

  ADOURN TO THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION ADVISORY BOARD MEETING

  A.  TRACY AUSTIN TOURNAMENT (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Morquecho stated that the schedule will be postponed due to multiple factors.
  The tournament is a doubles tournament which is currently restricted by Los Angeles
  County guidelines. An alternative date of late Fall or January is proposed by the
  subcommittee in coordination with Ms. Tracy Austin.

  VICE CHAIR POPE asked of the status of other tournaments such as the U.S. Open, that
  the subcommittee was waiting on to see if the doubles tournament could proceed. ACM
  Davis responded that if the U.S. Open occurs it may require additional coordination with
  Tracy Austin’s schedule then the Rolling Hills Estates doubles tournament may be
  possible. Information would be provided as it becomes available. Supervisor Morquecho
  added that the U.S. Open is moving forward with no audience spectators.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ noted that in regard to COVID-19 a second wave in September
  or October and a third wave in December or January is anticipated. Supervisor
  Morquecho responded that the County will release more information on the COVID-19
  situation in the coming weeks as it pertains to group gatherings. A subcommittee meeting
  has been scheduled for June 24, 2020.

  B.  PROPOSED HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE DATE

  Supervisor Morquecho provided a brief overview per the agenda material and provided
  additional information recently received by Los Angeles County Department of Public
  Health (DPC). A response for DPH was read which noted the consideration of
  postponement or cancelation of event and recommendations to restrict any pre-
  registration or day of registration gathering, prohibit fruit and water stations locations
  throughout the racecourse, and post-race vendor location

  ACM Davis stated that group gatherings are still not permitted and that eliminating the
  water stations in August would not be ideal for the race. If the August 8th date is approved
  by the Commission it will need to be recommended to the City Council for approval and
  then registration could start the following week.

  CHAIR PERSICHINA asked to clarify what a “virtual race” was. Supervisor Morquecho
  stated that a participant could run the distance from anywhere they are located and
  verification must be submitted by virtual map. Southbay Children’s Hospital will host a
  virtual race in July and will notify City staff of their findings. Websites can host this platform
  which can be used as a one stop shop for registration and getting tiered purchase levels.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
JUNE 15, 2020
   This would also allow UCLA Health to sponsor the event as they prefer a virtual race over
  an in person event.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA stated a virtual race would be best.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ stated since nothing has changed at this point he suggested
  bottled water at watering stations if the race ocurrs. He also suggested putting a waiver
  on the application to waive liability if COVID-19 is contracted at the race.

  CHAIR PERSICHINA stated the race can be pushed back to any date but that the August
  weather would be best for the race.

  VICE CHAIR POPE stated that September and October could limit chances of heat stroke
  and give staff more time to plan the event.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated the subcommittee reviewed the issues and is
  recommending August 8 be kept as the event date. He further explained that if the Health
  ORder is not lifted or loosened within one month of the event, then the City would look at
  an alternate date, including a virtual option.

  Supervisor Morquecho stated staff is on track with event planning process.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN stated it would be a lot of work if no one were to come.

  Supervisor Morquecho stated a survey could be sent to past participants but results may
  not provided in time to be brought back to the Commission .

  ACM Davis stated that due to current DPH restrictions, many other activities have been
  canceled, postponed or modified. She added that if August 8th is the date decided, staff
  would delay notifying the public by one week.

  CHAIR PERSICHINA stated if August 8th is not viable, October could be an alternative or
  that a virtual race could be implemented.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ stated that promoting a race on August 8th would send the wrong
  message to the public, for an event that may put people at risk. He is in favor of a virtual
  race over a physical one and expressed concern with having an in-person event at all this
  year. COMMISSIONER BAIN concurred and suggested that the City hold a virtual event
  only due to the risks associated with COVID-19.

  Supervisor Morquecho added that alternative ways to modify the race such as staggering
  race start times can be used if needed. ACM Davis added drive up packet pick-ups and
  virtual registration can be implemented to limit contact.

  CHAIR PERSICHINA stated this is new territory and that backing a race on August 8th
  could be a risk to the public and that a later date is preferred.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA to:

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
JUNE 15, 2020
   HOLD THE HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE AS A VIRTUAL RACE ON AUGUST 8TH.

  CHAIR PERSICHINA REQUESTED A ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES: Retz, Bain, Ciarolla

  NOES: Pope, Romanelli, Persichina

  ABSENT : McCormick

  ACM Davis stated that staff can take this vote to the City Council or the Commission may
  wish to continue deliberating toward a recommendation that is suitable to the majority of
  the Commission.

  CHAIR PERSICHINA stated that a date would be preferred. COMMISSIONER
  ROMANELLI stated that staff could follow Department of Health guidelines by the date of
  the event and keep the August 8 event date. COMMISSIONER RETZ stated that the
  current guidelines should be followed and schools’ reopening should also be looked at to
  see if the race should go forward.

  Member of the Public, Connie Smith, stated that gyms, day camps, some sports without
  audiences, television production, and short-term rentals are starting back up some
  restrictions. COMMISSIONER BAIN stated that these are applicable with proper
  disinfecting which is not in line with the concept of the race. ACM Davis stated that these
  also have limitations to how many people can gather at one time. She also noted that
  sports day camps are not permitted under the new order and that current guidelines are
  still somewhat unclear in some areas. She asked if there was an alternative date
  suggested by the Commission.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA asked if the date of the cancelled Portuguese Bend Horse
  Show could be used around September 9th.

  ACM Davis asked about the Conquer the Bridge Race but was told by staff it would be
  after Labor Day. It was noted by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI that the Conquer the
  Bridge Race was still being planned to move forward and is soliciting registrations
  currently.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA made a motion, seconded by CHAIR PERSICHINA to:

  HOLD THE HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE ON SEPTEMBER 12, 2020 WITH AN
  ADDED VIRTUAL RACE OPTION AND THE OPPORTUNITY TO CHANGE THE
  DATE IN ACCORDANCE WITH COUNTY GUIDELINES.

  CHAIR PERSICHINA REQUESTED A ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES: Ciarolla, Pope, Romanelli, Persichina

  NOES: Bain, Retz

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
JUNE 15, 2020
   ABSENT : McCormick

  Supervisor Morquecho asked if restrictions continue to be in place and prevent the in
  person dates, would the Commission recommend a virtual race be held in its place or the
  event cancelled all together. The Commission stated a virtual alternative be preferred to
  cancelation of the event.

  There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA so ordered.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS (This item was taken out of order)

  A.  PVPLC ANNUAL REPORT (VERBAL REPORT)

  Staff Members Connie Smith and Alex Kovary from the Palos Verdes Peninsula Land
  Conservancy (PVPLC) provided a brief overview of the Nature Center Annual Report and
  nearby preserve. The Nature Center provides school trips, education, and restoration
  projects to parts of the 1600 acre 42 miles of trails open to the public. In 2019 traffic was
  increased to the Nature Center by 20% which is about 1,000 more visitors. Sierra Club
  also brings in visitors from outside the area. Relationships with schools along PV Drive
  North are in place to increase visitation to the Nature Center. Superintendent Goldsmith
  has also aided in improving signage throughout the Nature Center and nearby trails.
  Online and digital outreach has also improved. The numbers for 2020 will not look like
  2019 as the Nature Center has been closed since mid-February due to COVID-19
  restrictions. Third grade naturalist numbers have been steady as docents from the Nature
  Center visit local third graders virtually, to educate them in four lessons about wildlife and
  plant life in the area. Alex Kovary stated that reopening the Nature Center will depend on
  the County guidelines. High touch areas have been replaced with digital replacements.
  COMMISSIONER RETZ asked for contact information.

  9.  RECONVENE TO PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING

  CHAIR PERSICHINA made a motion,

  RECONVENE TO THE PARK AND ACITIVITIES COMMITTEE MEETING

  There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA so ordered.

  10.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK REPORTS

  COMMISSIONER RETZ noted a sign was loose near the Nature Center. Superintendent
  Goldsmith stated it will be addressed.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
JUNE 15, 2020
   11.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  COVID-19 UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  ACM Davis stated that Friday Los Angeles County Department of Public Health (DPH)
  further opened some sectors, including Day Camps, hair salons, and Professional sports
  with limitations. Movie theaters and nail salons and other close grooming businesses
  have not been opened. Restaurants are open with capacity limitations, but the City has
  worked with local restaurants to allow no-fee permits for outdoor seating. Park facilities
  trails are still open but playgrounds, sports fields and group gatherings are still not allowed
  so no park permits have been issued. Small horse shows have been advocated by the
  City to DPH as staff believes they can be run safely. Staff is hopeful to have small horse
  shows going by July but will work closely within DPH guidelines. Silver Spur Little League
  has been cautious and have not held practices. Smaller little league practices have been
  observed in parks by staff but no citations have been given, just education on the situation.
  Basketball and volleyball courts are still closed. Tennis courts only allow for single play
  and a mask is required to be worn in between courts. Tennis instructor Bob has come
  back to teach in limited capacity of two students per instructor and masks being worn at
  all times. An upcoming City Celebration subcommittee meeting will determine the date of
  the 2020 event. June and July movie nights have been canceled but an alternative drive-
  in option has been proposed for August. The goal is not to cancel the movie night.

  ACM Davis stated that staff is looking into refunding tennis memberships for the time the
  courts were closed from mid-March through mid-May which would be approximately
  $1,600 in refunds. Staff is working with the Finance Director to see if a refund or credit for
  next year would be suitable. VICE CHAIR POPE stated the refunds could be donated to
  the Pepper Tree Foundation if tennis members would allow.

  B.  MAYOR’S BREAKFAST RIDE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Morquecho stated the proposed July 4th would not be viable due to DPH
  guidelines and that the August 8 date is a suggested alternative depending on the Race
  event. The Ridewould still take place but would forgo the Scout breakfast. ACM Davis
  stated that having the event on July 4 would limit the riders on the trail to only foru which
  would not provide the community aspect to the event. Staff is expecting to have more
  information from the DPH later in the month or July to see if these restrictions are lifted.

  12.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF MAY 26 2020

  Received and filed

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF JUNE 9, 2020 BUDGET STUDY SESSION

  Received and filed

  C.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF JUNE 9, 2020

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
JUNE 15, 2020
   Received and filed

  13.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  CITY CELEBRATION

  Supervisor Morquecho stated the subcommittee meeting will happen soon to discuss the
  event.

  B.  HOLIDAY PARADE OF LIGHTS

  There being no objection, VICE CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  14.  PARK TOURS

  Superintendent Goldsmith provided a brief overview per agenda material. Superintendent
  Goldsmith added that the potential Scout project on the Nature Center trail proposed by
  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK has not been taken up by any Scout group yet.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked about the red marked workout stations at Highridge
  Park. Superintendent Goldsmith stated that they will be taken net week due to old age
  and backfilled. The only station that gets use is the pull up bar near the garage area.

  ACM Davis stated that the Nature Center re-design is coming along. She added that staff
  is seeking the Commission’s availability for a meeting on June 22 at 6pm Merrill Gardens,
  a commercial district, would like to submit a landscape plan through Zoom so that the
  Commission could review.

  The Park and Activities Commission toured George F Canyon Nature preserve trail and
  Dapplegray Park noted the following:

  •  Path to Learning Tree needs to be trimmed back

  15.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISISONER RETZ to,

  ADJOURN THE MEETING AT 7:19 PM TO THE NEXT ADJOURNED PARK AND
  ACTIVITIES MEETING ON JULY 20, 2020 AT 6:00 P.M., WHICH WILL MEET
  AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK, 25851 HAWTHORNE BLVD., ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES.

  There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  7
JUNE 15, 2020
